evidence.record_quote: The Electronic Poetry Center ( EPC ), is an online resource for digital poetry .

atoms.reference: Loss Pequeño Glazier, Director and Founder; Charles Bernstein, Editor and Co-founder; Al Filreis, Publisher.
Founded at Buffalo in 1995 (its About page); 10 July 1994 (Wikipedia).

evidence.record_quote: EPC was founed by Loss Peqeño Glazier, with Charles Bernstein, at the Poetics Program of SUNY-Buffalo in 1995.
It was founded on July 10, 1994 by Loss Pequeño Glazier and Charles Bernstein , of the Poetics Program at The State University of New York at Buffalo

atoms.reference: The first comprehensive Internet archive of its kind for poetry and poetics, with a Digital Library, E-Poetry and Author libraries.

evidence.record_quote: The site was the first comprehensive Internet archive of its kind for poetry and poetics.
EPC makes extensive resources available through its Digital Library, E-Poetry and Author libraries.

atoms.reference: Author pages, digitized books and journal runs (Sulfur), and the archives of the Buffalo Poetics Program (1991 to 2003) and the Poetics List (1993 to 2014).

evidence.record_quote: Author Pages : Mina Loy and Bill Keith
We also house the archives of the Buffalo Poetics Program from its fouding in 1991 to 2003 and of the Poetics List (1993-2014), the first poetry listserv discussion group.

atoms.reference: To make available a wide range of resources centered on digital and contemporary formally innovative poetries, new media writing and literary programming.

atoms.span: Overview: Electronic Poetry Center (EPC) is an online resource for digital poetry
Founded: July 10, 1994, by Loss Pequeño Glazier and Charles Bernstein.
is a major online archive and resource gateway for digital, experimental, and avant-garde poetry.
Author Libraries: Curated collections of contemporary poet pages containing biographies, photos, essays, and links to online works.
Origin: Created as part of the Poetics Program at the State University of New York (SUNY) at Buffalo.

observations.notes: The center composed accurately at its grain from its Wikipedia article, with that article's founding date and its Buffalo frame. Its move to Penn and the archives of the Poetics Program and the Poetics List, on its own About page, are absent.
